answer: Dawn-scheduled unique-work auction. Each identity must win a scarce daily task slot by submitting verifiably unique computation before dawn; duplicates are discarded. Slots are hashed into a public shale-anchored ledger, so cloning requires winning additional slots at rising clearing prices. An attacker pays the full market cost per clone, every day, while honest agents amortize one slot across sustained work. A walnut-sized audit sample per epoch confirms uniqueness.
